result.title: LaplaceDiag: Fault Diagnosis through Changes in Learned Actuator Effects
result.summary: Identifying faulty components from sensor anomalies is difficult because fault effects can propagate through a plant and different faults can produce similar observations. Detailed component models and labeled fault examples may also be unavailable. We introduce LaplaceDiag, a data-driven method that uses changes in actuator effects to narrow the search for faulty equipment. Actuators act on specific devices and mechanisms, so their changed effects can provide clues to root causes. LaplaceDiag learns a healthy plant model with LaplaceNet, a neural network that operates in Laplace space. It separates nonlinear prediction based on measured history from an explicit matrix that describes how actuator values affect sensor values. Keeping the history predictor fixed allows current actuator effects to be estimated by linear regression without retraining the neural network. Comparison with a healthy reference accounts for estimation uncertainty and normal variation to detect changes and generate actuator-related diagnostic hypotheses. The method supports online and offline diagnosis, providing an intermediate step between anomaly detection and identifying faulty components. We successfully evaluate LaplaceDiag on two datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LaplaceDiag：用 LaplaceNet 在 Laplace 空间学习健康工况模型，把基于历史测量的非线性预测与描述执行器对传感器影响的显式矩阵分离；固定历史预测器后可用线性回归估计当前执行器效应，再与健康参考比较并计入估计不确定性，从而检测变化、生成部件级诊断假设。
AI.relevance_reason: 属工业故障诊断远领域，但其「固定历史预测器 + 显式效应矩阵」的解耦与不确定性驱动的假设筛选，可能为 LVR 中内部状态更新与视觉证据贡献的分离、候选假设生成及停止决策提供概念线索，需进一步核查。
